arxiv-2111-05865.title: MATBG as Topological Heavy Fermion: I. Exact Mapping and Correlated Insulators
arxiv-2111-05865.creator: Zhi-Da Song, B. Andrei Bernevig
arxiv-2111-05865.description: Abstract Magic-angle ( θ = 1.05 ∘ \theta=1.05^{\circ} ) twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG) has shown two seemingly contradictory characters: the localization and quantum-dot-like behavior in STM experiments, and delocalization in transport experiments. We construct a model, which naturally captures the two aspects, from the Bistritzer-MacDonald (BM) model in a first principle spirit .

arxiv-2407-05902.title: Towards Photon-Number-Encoded High-dimensional Entanglement from a Sequentially Excited Quantum Three-Level System
arxiv-2407-05902.creator: Daniel A. Vajner, Nils D. Kewitz, Martin von Helversen, Stephen C. Wein, Yusuf Karli, Florian Kappe, Vikas Remesh, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Armando Rastelli, Gregor Weihs, Carlos Anton-Solanas, Tobias Heindel
arxiv-2407-05902.description: Abstract The sequential resonant excitation of a 2-level quantum system results in the emission of a state of light showing time-entanglement encoded in the photon-number-basis – notions that can be extended to 3-level quantum systems as discussed in a recent proposal [ 1 ] .

arxiv-2507-04092.title: Adaptive Designs in Fast-Track Registration Processes
arxiv-2507-04092.creator: Liane Kluge, Werner Brannath
arxiv-2507-04092.description: Abstract Fast-track procedures play an important role in the context of conditional registration of health products, such as conditional approval processes and listing processes for digital health applications. Fast-track procedures offer the potential for earlier patient access to innovative products. They involve two registration steps. The applicants can apply first for conditional registration.

arxiv-2512-11922.title: Vibe Coding in Practice: Flow, Technical Debt, and Guidelines for Sustainable Use

arxiv-2512-11922.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Muhammad Waseem, Aakash Ahmad, Kai-Kristian Kemell, Jussi Rasku, Sami Lahti, Kalle Mäkelä, Pekka Abrahamsson. Vibe Coding (VC) is a form of software development assisted by generative AI, in which developers describe the intended functionality or logic via natural language prompts, and the AI system generates the corresponding source code. VC can be used for rapid prototyping or developing the Minimum Viable Products (MVPs); however, it may introduce several risks throughout the software development life cycle.

pmc-11448338.description: AimsThere is scarce knowledge about the association between social factors and mid-term outcome in older patients undergoing transaortic valve implantation (TAVI). pmc-11692753.title: OPTIMIZING VOLUNTARY WORK DESIGN FOR HEALTHY AGING: RETHINKING VOLUNTEER ENGAGEMENT

pmc-11692753.description: While existing research primarily focuses on the health benefits of volunteering in terms of quantity (e.g., participation or volunteer hours), the psychosocial aspects of role engagement in volunteering and its impact on healthy aging remain underexplored. Additionally, insights on establishing a supportive volunteering environment at the organizational level to facilitate healthy aging are lacking.

pmc-11714136.title: Feasibility of Training Family Caregivers of People Living with Dementia Online to Deliver Life Review Depression Intervention at Home
pmc-11714136.creator: Christina E Miyawaki, Erin D Bouldin, Angela McClellan
pmc-11714136.description: BackgroundDue to the high prevalence of depressive symptoms and dementia in older Americans (≥65 years), we trained unpaid family caregivers in an evidence‐based life review depression intervention virtually via Zoom and produced positive outcomes. The objective of this study was to examine the feasibility of training caregivers via online video and delivering the intervention at home.

pmc-13326243.creator: Ning Zhu, Qinghua Liu, Yuchen Chang, Yu Zhang
pmc-13326243.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThis study aimed to compare the accuracy and efficiency of implant-site preparation and placement between conventional serial drilling and trephine drilling, with assistance from an implant robot, on varying bone surface inclinations.MethodsA total of 80 implants were placed in a standard polyurethane model using the two drilling methods (conventional serial drilling and trephine drilling) with four different bone surface inclinations (0°, 15°, 30°, 45°), resulting in eight sub-groups. pmc-13416106.creator: Beibei Tang, Keke Li, Wanyu Chen, Juanjuan Xiao, Qiuhong Duan, Feng Zhu
pmc-13416106.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are central to immune regulation, preventing excessive immune responses, maintaining immune tolerance, and modulating inflammatory microenvironments. Dysregulation of Treg development, differentiation, proliferation, or function contributes significantly to autoimmune diseases, inflammatory disorders, and tumor immune evasion. Protein kinases, key mediators of cellular signaling, regulate diverse processes including motility, metabolism, transport, and cell cycle progression; their emerging roles in immune regulation make them promising therapeutic targets for inflammatory diseases, autoimmunity, and immunotherapy-treated cancers.

uslaw-usc-t50-s2203.title: 50 U.S.C. § 2203 — Report on previous transfers
uslaw-usc-t50-s2203.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t50-s2203.description: United States Code, Title 50 (War And National Defense); Chapter 39 (Spoils Of War). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Not later than 90 days after April 30, 1994, the President shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report describing any spoils of war obtained subsequent to August 2, 1990 that were transferred to any party, including any government, group, or person.
